scenarios.name: cooling_coil_doing_its_job
scenarios.description: Minimum-OA mechanical cooling on a warm day: a 24 °C mixture leaves the coil at 13 °C. SAT is 11 °C below MAT, the sign the rule expects in every cooling-side state, so there is nothing to report

scenarios.name: fan_heat_with_no_cooling_demand
scenarios.description: SAT sits 1.5 °C above MAT with the coil idle — about what the supply fan alone adds (dTSF = 1 °C) plus a fraction of the sensor allowances. The 5 °C threshold is built to absorb exactly this case, so the rule stays silent

scenarios.name: gap_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge: SAT − MAT = 5.0 °C exactly, the full eSAT + eMAT + dTSF allowance. `gapBig` is a strict `>`, so a gap sitting precisely on the composed allowance reads healthy

scenarios.name: gap_just_over_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge, other side: SAT − MAT = 5.1 °C clears the strict comparison and the alarm asserts one alarm_delay (1800 s) later

scenarios.name: heat_stuck_on_during_mechanical_cooling
scenarios.description: The unit is in a cooling state and the air still gains 9 °C crossing the AHU — a gas or electric heating stage stuck on, or a heating valve leaking through. Air cannot warm itself, so this is the CLU-01 waste case: energy added and removed on the same stream

scenarios.name: mat_sensor_reading_low
scenarios.description: A plausible SAT of 18 °C against a MAT of 12 °C on a day with no 12 °C air anywhere in the building — the same 6 °C violation, but here the mixed-air sensor is what is wrong. The rule reports the contradiction; it cannot say which of the two sensors is lying

scenarios.name: transient_clears_before_alarm_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: the gap holds at 9 °C for 1200 s while a heating stage finishes its off-cycle purge, then SAT drops to 15 °C. Anything shorter than alarm_delay never reaches the operator

scenarios.name: fault_clears_on_recovery
scenarios.description: A sustained 9 °C gap alarms at 1800 s; the stuck heating stage is switched off at t = 3000 and SAT falls to 14 °C. `TrueDelay` has no off-delay, so the alarm drops on that tick

scenarios.name: oscillating_gap_never_alarms
scenarios.description: A staging heater cycling on a 10-minute period drives the gap between 9 °C and 0 °C. Its mean is well outside the threshold and G36's 5-minute rolling average would report the fault, but persistence restarts on every compliant tick, so this rule stays silent — the limit of substituting TrueDelay for averaging (see Deviations)
